title: Which fictional caption tool should a solo creator trial?
summary: Trial QuillNest first: its supplied product card meets the stated budget, project count, and caption-export needs. The comparison does not establish real pricing or caption quality.
assumptions: Compare only the advertised monthly plans in the supplied fictional snippets; do not consider discounts or annual billing.
limitations: All evidence is fictional, user-provided text; no product page was accessed or independently verified.
Neither product card establishes caption accuracy, and the creator has tested neither tool.

data.question: Which supplied fictional tool is the better first trial for a solo creator making four videos monthly with an AUD 25 budget and a need for caption export?
data.scope: A comparison of advertised fit using exactly three provided snippets, without current-price verification or a purchase recommendation.
data.answer: QuillNest is the better first trial under the supplied constraints: the stated AUD 19 monthly plan includes six projects and caption export. ClipHarbor's stated AUD 29 plan exceeds the budget. Test caption accuracy before deciding to pay.

findings.text: The supplied QuillNest card advertises AUD 19 per month, six projects, caption export, one user, and a seven-day trial.
The supplied ClipHarbor card advertises AUD 29 per month, twenty projects, caption export, one user, and a seven-day trial.
Against the user's AUD 25 budget and four-video workload, QuillNest's advertised plan fits; ClipHarbor costs AUD 4 over budget and offers capacity the stated workload does not require.
Neither card describes accuracy, and the creator's supplied note says neither tool has been tested.
QuillNest may be sufficient for the creator's actual caption workflow; one trial video could reveal unacceptable transcription errors or export friction.
